summary: Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University and the University of Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He taught at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, the University of Leipzig, and held an Ordinarius post at Heidelberg University (1877).

Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology, completing his doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. His career included posts at the University of Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Zürich, University of Vienna, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and a professorship at the University of Göttingen (1855).

Hermann Usener worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Munich, and Bonn. His career included posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Halle-Wittenberg and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and August Friedrich Pott. He held posts at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and Berlin as comparative philology chair (1872).

Hermann von Schlagintweit was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at the University of Munich (~1844–1848). He held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854) and was a member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Hermanus Johannes de Graaf was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1919–1926) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927–1930).

Heymann Steinthal was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847) and later held posts at Frederick William University Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin (~1850–1899), and Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He also held a researcher post at Taisho University, attested in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, with Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He held a professorship at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed a PhD at Tohoku University. Kurita held a lecturer post at Aichi Prefectural University, attested in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Delhi. Kiyoshima held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

Hideki Yukawa studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and Osaka University (~1934–1938). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1932–1970), Osaka University (~1933–1939), the University of Tokyo (~1939–1950), and Columbia University (~1949–1953).
Hidemasa Nagata was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1952–1961) and later held an academic post there from around 1966 to 1996.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He held posts at Tokyo, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Women's University (~1950–1974).
Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hakuju Ui. He held a professorship at Nagoya University, attested in 1968–1969.

Hidenori S. Sakuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at Shitennoji University, Taisho University, and University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yamagata Higher School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He held faculty posts at Waseda University (1960–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1976–1998).

Hideomi Yaita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. Yaita held posts at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1975–1979) and held an academic post at Hitotsubashi University (~1996–2020).
